{{Short description|Lemma in control theory}}
In [[control theory]] and in particular when studying the properties of a [[linear time-invariant]] system in [[state space]] form, the '''Hautus lemma''' (after Malo L. J. Hautus), also commonly known as the '''Popov-Belevitch-Hautus test''' or '''PBH test''',<ref name=":0">{{cite book |last1=Hespanha |first1=Joao |title=Linear Systems Theory |date=2018 |publisher=Princeton University Press |isbn=9780691179575 |edition=Second}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Bernstein |first1=Dennis S. |title=Scalar, Vector, and Matrix Mathematics: Theory, Facts, and Formulas |date=2018 |publisher=Princeton University Press |isbn=9780691151205 |edition=Revised and expanded}}</ref> gives equivalent conditions for certain properties of control systems. 

A special case of this result appeared first in 1963 in a paper by [[Elmer G. Gilbert]],<ref name=":0" /> and was later expanded to the current PBH test with contributions by [[Vasile M. Popov]] in 1966,<ref>{{cite book |last=Popov |first=Vasile Mihai |title=Hiperstabilitatea sistemelor automate |publisher=Editura Academiei Republicii Socialiste România |year=1966 |trans-title=Hyperstability of Control Systems}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Popov |first=V.M. |title=Hyperstability of Control Systems |publisher=Springer-Verlag |year=1973 |location=Berlin}}</ref> [[Vitold Belevitch]] in 1968,<ref name=":1">{{cite book |last=Belevitch |first=V. |title=Classical Network Theory |publisher=Holden–Day |year=1968 |location=San Francisco}}</ref> and Malo Hautus in 1969,<ref name=":1" /> who emphasized its applicability in proving results for linear time-invariant systems. 

==Statement==
There exist multiple forms of the lemma:
===Hautus Lemma for controllability===
The Hautus lemma for controllability says that given a square matrix <math>\mathbf{A}\in M_n(\Re)</math> and a <math>\mathbf{B}\in M_{n\times m}(\Re)</math> the following are equivalent:
# The pair <math>(\mathbf{A},\mathbf{B})</math> is [[controllable]]
# For all <math>\lambda\in\mathbb{C}</math> it holds that <math>\operatorname{rank}[\lambda \mathbf{I}-\mathbf{A},\mathbf{B}]=n</math>
# For all <math>\lambda\in\mathbb{C}</math> that are eigenvalues of <math>\mathbf{A}</math> it holds that <math>\operatorname{rank}[\lambda \mathbf{I}-\mathbf{A},\mathbf{B}]=n</math>

===Hautus Lemma for stabilizability===
The Hautus lemma for stabilizability says that given a square matrix <math>\mathbf{A}\in M_n(\Re)</math> and a <math>\mathbf{B}\in M_{n\times m}(\Re)</math> the following are equivalent:
# The pair <math>(\mathbf{A},\mathbf{B})</math> is [[Stabilizability|stabilizable]]
# For all <math>\lambda\in\mathbb{C}</math> that are eigenvalues of <math>\mathbf{A}</math> and for which <math>\Re(\lambda)\ge 0</math> it holds that <math>\operatorname{rank}[\lambda \mathbf{I}-\mathbf{A},\mathbf{B}]=n</math>
===Hautus Lemma for observability===
The Hautus lemma for observability says that given a square matrix <math>\mathbf{A}\in M_n(\Re)</math> and a <math>\mathbf{C}\in M_{m\times n}(\Re)</math> the following are equivalent:
# The pair <math>(\mathbf{A},\mathbf{C})</math> is [[Observability|observable]].
# For all <math>\lambda\in\mathbb{C}</math> it holds that <math>\operatorname{rank}[\lambda \mathbf{I}-\mathbf{A};\mathbf{C}]=n</math>
# For all <math>\lambda\in\mathbb{C}</math> that are eigenvalues of <math>\mathbf{A}</math> it holds that <math>\operatorname{rank}[\lambda \mathbf{I}-\mathbf{A};\mathbf{C}]=n</math>

===Hautus Lemma for detectability===
The Hautus lemma for detectability says that given a square matrix <math>\mathbf{A}\in M_n(\Re)</math> and a <math>\mathbf{C}\in M_{m\times n}(\Re)</math> the following are equivalent:
# The pair <math>(\mathbf{A},\mathbf{C})</math> is [[Detectability|detectable]]
# For all <math>\lambda\in\mathbb{C}</math> that are eigenvalues of <math>\mathbf{A}</math> and for which <math>\Re(\lambda)\ge 0</math> it holds that <math>\operatorname{rank}[\lambda \mathbf{I}-\mathbf{A};\mathbf{C}]=n</math>
